A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain 26 readable pages, including Appendices A–E. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the text, equations, table, and figures without material gaps.

before.justification: v3 reports original offline and online adversarial segmentation experiments, comparisons with U-Net in Table 1, and two-moons clustering experiments in Appendix E.

after.justification: v4 retains the original segmentation and clustering experiments, including Table 1 and the numerical results in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same Lovász subgradient, Gaussian gradient estimator, and projected extragradient updates. The online adaptation and oracle variants in Appendix D are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic offline and online adversarial image segmentation and two-moons clustering tasks in Section 4 and Appendix E.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same supervised U-Net and semi-supervised U-Net comparators. No comparison method is added, removed, or revised.

E3.justification: Experimental settings remain identical, including U-Net training on 3,000 images and Appendix E.2's thresholding and frame-averaging rules: Algorithm 1 excludes the first 120 frames, while U-Net metrics use all frames.

E4.justification: The adversarial-budget sensitivity studies for segmentation and clustering in Appendices E.1 and E.3, including Figures 3 and 7–9, are unchanged. No ablation or robustness analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report 10 independent runs for Algorithm 1 and relative variation of order 10^-4 in Appendix E.2. Repeated-run and uncertainty reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains identical values, including average IoU of 0.975, 0.905, and 0.847 for Algorithm 1, supervised U-Net, and semi-supervised U-Net, respectively. Figures 1–12 and their reported findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, saddle-point propositions, and Theorems 3.2 and 3.6 are unchanged. Appendices A–D retain the same mathematical examples, proofs, and derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty, offline convergence, online duality-gap, and segmentation-performance claims.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the explanations of budget-dependent robustness, transient cost oscillations, and online tracking. Qualifications concerning the U-Net comparison and sensitivity to changing cost functions in Appendix E.2 are unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation parameters, hardware disclosures, data-generation details, and code/package access information in Section 4 and Appendix E remain identical.

R1.justification: Farzin et al. (2025d) becomes Farzin et al. (2026) for the same titled work, 'Minimisation of quasar-convex functions using random zeroth-order oracles,' with an updated author list and TMLR publication metadata. This is a bibliographic update; cited-work membership and research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 replaces the ICML/PMLR proceedings and copyright footer with 'Preprint. September 9, 2026.' It also updates the arXiv version/date and one reference's bibliographic text and citation year. Scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The shorter publication footer and expanded reference produce limited text reflow on pages 1–3 and 10–11, including moving the Ronneberger reference onto page 11. Table 1 and all figures retain their content and layout.

improvement.justification: v4 changes the publication notice and updates an existing reference, with minor accompanying reflow. The method, proofs, experimental evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations—including all appendices—remain unchanged. These editorial updates do not establish a meaningful overall quality gain or loss.
